info.title: automaton
info.description: Automaton CLI — deploy apps, manage runners, publish versions

commands.name: catalog
commands.description: Create and build an apps repository for use as a catalog source, and manage the server's catalog sources

commands.name: init
commands.description: Write the files of a new apps repository (example app, catalog list, CI workflow, README); nothing is pushed

arguments.name: DIRECTORY
arguments.description: Folder to create the repository files in (empty or new) [default: .]

commands.name: build
commands.description: Generate catalog.json from catalog-apps.json and each app's automaton.json

options.name: --repo
options.description: Repository as owner/name (default: "repo" in catalog-apps.json, then $GITHUB_REPOSITORY)

options.name: --out
options.description: Write the catalog here (default: catalog.json in the folder)

options.name: --validate
options.description: Only check the entries; write nothing

arguments.name: DIRECTORY
arguments.description: The apps repository folder (needs catalog-apps.json, and git history for the pinned commits) [default: .]

commands.name: sources
commands.description: Manage the catalog sources of the server (system administrator): list, add, enable, disable, remove

commands.name: list
commands.description:
List the catalog sources and whether each is used.
Example: automaton catalog sources list

options.name: --json
options.description: Print the result as JSON (for agents)

commands.name: add
commands.description:
Add a catalog source.
Public:  automaton catalog sources add https://github.com/acme/apps
Private: automaton catalog sources add https://github.com/acme/apps --private --token-file ~/catalog-token
Check first: add --dry-run. A token is a fine-grained, read-only Contents token for that one repository.

options.name: --name
options.description: How the source is shown in the Catalog (default: the repository name)

options.name: --private
options.description: The repository is private: read its token from --token-file, --token-stdin or a hidden prompt

options.name: --token-file
options.description: File that holds the read token of a private repository (never pass a token as an argument)

options.name: --token-stdin
options.description: Read the token from standard input

options.name: --dry-run
options.description: Check the repository, branch, catalog.json and token and print what would be added; add nothing

options.name: --json
options.description: Print the result as JSON (for agents)

arguments.name: REPOSITORY
arguments.description: owner/name or https://github.com/owner/name

commands.name: enable
commands.description:
Use a catalog source.
Example: automaton catalog sources enable <id>

options.name: --json
options.description: Print the result as JSON (for agents)

arguments.name: ID
arguments.description: The source id from automaton catalog sources list

commands.name: disable
commands.description:
Stop using a catalog source.
Example: automaton catalog sources disable <id>

options.name: --json
options.description: Print the result as JSON (for agents)

arguments.name: ID
arguments.description: The source id from automaton catalog sources list

commands.name: remove
commands.description:
Remove a catalog source and its saved catalog; apps already installed keep running.
Example: automaton catalog sources remove <id>

options.name: --json
options.description: Print the result as JSON (for agents)

arguments.name: ID
arguments.description: The source id from automaton catalog sources list
